long_biography.plain_text:
Robert Sands grew up around the Canandaigua winery established by his father, Marvin. Summer jobs took him inside the operation, moving hoses, cleaning tanks and removing crystallized sugar from railcars. After studying philosophy at Skidmore College and law at Pace University, he spent two years with a Rochester law firm before joining the family company as general counsel in 1986.

His legal brief centred on acquisitions, opening a path through international management, group presidency and operating leadership. Sands succeeded his brother Richard as chief executive in 2007. During his twelve-year tenure, Constellation secured the United States rights to the Modelo and Corona portfolio, built production capacity in Mexico and concentrated its brands toward premium categories. He later chaired the board and now serves as a non-management director.
